recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the R5 Library profiles in core; any further maintenance of those profile definitions belongs in the owning external IGs or in a separate bounded reconciliation for FHIR-48393's broader profile-removal scope.
issue_request: FHIR-28940 was a Published/Persuasive CDS issue for R5 requesting Library profiles from the Quality Measure IG: Executable, Publishable, and Computable Library, with the final resolution also adding ModuleDefinition and ModelInfo Library profiles.
initial_application: FHIR-I minutes moved the tracker to CDS. Source history shows commit bd5308f495121a1d68556930e5c065c67189badb applying J#28940 by adding Library profile StructureDefinitions and Library CQF implementation guide entries, so the seed was materially applied before R5.
additional_context: Later Applied/Persuasive issue FHIR-48393 directed removal of profile definitions from the base specification for R6, listing the relevant Library profiles as already moved to Using CQL With FHIR or CRMI. Commit 571498e2b2959573e07980c9117923b42624e3a1 deleted the Library profile files and removed Library package entries. A CDS agenda records the broader TSC direction that resource profiles should not remain in the base FHIR specification.
reconciliation: The current Library resource remains active in source/fhir.ini, but the current core source intentionally has no Library profile StructureDefinition files and source/library/list-Library-packs.xml has no entries. Restoring the FHIR-28940 profiles in core would contradict the later FHIR-48393 decision, so an empty no-change audit commit was published.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied CDS issue removed the relevant Library profiles from the base specification and moved them to external IG ownership.
